macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global markets steadied after renewed Middle East tensions and swings in oil
items.summary: Reuters and Bloomberg reported that U.S. strikes on Iran and related geopolitical risks kept oil volatile and pressured risk assets, while global equities and futures rebounded modestly as oil retreated from earlier highs. Asian stocks were also described as poised to fall for a second day amid a chip-sector selloff.

items.title: ECB policymakers signaled a cautious but still hawkish inflation stance
items.summary: Reuters reported that ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane described the euro area as facing a moderate inflation shock, saying policy should remain cautious while inflation is expected to stay above 3% for the rest of the year. ECB policymaker Pierre Wunsch also said another rate hike could still be possible if underlying euro-zone inflation keeps broadening beyond energy.

items.title: Japan bond yields hit multi-decade highs as inflation and fiscal concerns build
items.summary: Reuters reported that the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield reached a 30-year high amid rising oil prices and renewed inflation concerns. Bloomberg added that Japan’s bank lending rose at the fastest pace since the Covid era, reinforcing expectations that the Bank of Japan has room to keep tightening.

items.title: IMF cut its 2026 global growth outlook on Iran-war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF reduced its 2026 world growth forecast to 3%, citing economic spillovers from the Iran war, while noting that AI-related demand partly offsets the energy shock. This added to broader concern that higher energy costs could slow global activity.

items.title: Asian markets were set to weaken as tech shares sold off
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that stocks in Asia were poised to drop for a second day as chipmakers led a regional selloff, with oil, bond yields, and geopolitical risk shaping sentiment. MarketScreener also highlighted mixed regional moves, including a weaker Nikkei and firmer Topix tied to the oil move.

items.title: Market calendar pointed to key U.S. data and Fed balance-sheet updates
items.summary: The economic calendar showed recent U.S. Federal Reserve balance-sheet and reserve-balance releases, with investors watching upcoming labor and services data for clues on the Fed path. A market-video roundup also said traders were focused on JOLTS, ISM services PMI, and Friday payrolls.

items.title: European macro data remained mixed, with stronger German orders and firmer UK retail sales
items.summary: Reuters’ Europe coverage said German industrial orders rose more than expected in May and UK new car sales increased 11% in June, suggesting some resilience in activity. The same feed also noted higher UK government borrowing in May as inflation lifted debt-service costs.

items.title: China inflation and trade data pointed to persistent price pressures
items.summary: Reuters reported that China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. Al Jazeera separately highlighted a widening trade imbalance as imports outpaced exports, underscoring an uneven recovery.

items.title: Company-specific moves included Samsung strength and chip-sector volatility
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour list showed Samsung Electronics among the most mentioned names with an 8.22% gain, while broader market commentary pointed to weakness in semiconductors and other tech stocks in Asia. The mix suggested heavy rotation within the sector rather than a uniform move across equities.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $63K as crypto markets soften
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $63,057, while Ethereum hovered around $1,862 and the total crypto market cap stood at about $2.17 trillion. Liquidations fell sharply to about $95.9 million, indicating calmer trading after recent volatility.

items.title: Coldcard wallet exploit drains about 388.9 BTC in a fourth attack wave
items.summary: A new attack wave reportedly hit 462 addresses and drained roughly 388.9 BTC, underscoring ongoing wallet-security risks for self-custodied crypto users. The incident also contributed to broader market caution.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as easing oil prices support risk appetite
items.summary: Bitcoin moved back above $63,000 as softer oil prices improved risk sentiment in crypto markets. Several market trackers also flagged mixed ETF flow dynamics and renewed attention on large holders.

items.title: Strategy bitcoin policy draws fresh scrutiny after reported losses
items.summary: Market coverage says Strategy’s updated policy on selling bitcoin has been criticized as introducing avoidable risk, while the company is also dealing with reported quarterly losses tied to bitcoin price declines. The issue has become a prominent talking point for market participants.

items.title: U.S. crypto regulation advances as Senate races toward CLARITY Act vote
items.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Senate to move quickly on the CLARITY Act, highlighting pressure around the bill’s timeline. The debate remains one of the most significant regulatory developments in the crypto sector.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong’s SFC reportedly forced crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, signaling a continued push for stronger operational security standards. The move is part of a broader wave of regional regulatory tightening.

items.title: Kraken seeks a European banking license
items.summary: Kraken is reportedly pursuing a European banking license as it expands its regulatory footprint in the region. The move reflects growing competition among major exchanges to secure formal banking access.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36 million Nevada factory for Bitcoin mining
items.summary: Bitdeer announced a new Nevada facility aimed at supporting Bitcoin mining operations. The project adds to ongoing investment in mining infrastructure despite a cautious market backdrop.

items.title: XRP gains attention as SWIFT taps Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments
items.summary: XRP-related coverage highlighted renewed interest after SWIFT reportedly worked with Ripple-linked banks on blockchain payments. The development has fueled speculation about enterprise adoption trends.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools. The release intensifies competition in workplace automation with rivals such as Anthropic and Meta.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI also introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The launch points to continued investment in lower-latency, multimodal AI experiences.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 to developers
items.summary: Meta launched developer access to Muse Spark 1.1 through a public API preview, positioning the model as a more capable option for advanced coding and multimodal reasoning. The move brings Meta more directly into competition with OpenAI and Anthropic in paid model access.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and aiming it at coding and agentic workflows. The model rollout underscores the accelerating race among major AI labs to improve practical task execution.

items.title: Meta announces new data center in Alberta to expand AI compute
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support growing AI infrastructure needs. The announcement reflects the broader industry trend toward aggressive compute expansion.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights continued governance-focused differentiation among leading AI firms.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI in copyright dispute
items.summary: A group of newspapers led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence in a copyright case. The filing adds to the legal pressure surrounding AI training data and publisher rights.

items.title: Ollama raises $65M Series B for local model tooling
items.summary: Ollama, a developer tool for running open-weight AI models locally, raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Venture. The round signals continued investor interest in infrastructure for open model deployment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Nintendo reveals Splatoon Raiders release date during Direct
items.summary: Nintendo used a Splatoon Raiders Direct to announce that the game will launch exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2 on July 23. The presentation also included fresh details about the spinoff.

items.title: Bethesda confirms Oblivion Remastered is coming to Switch 2
items.summary: Bethesda Softworks has confirmed that The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered will launch on Switch 2 on August 11, 2026. This is one of the most notable platform-release announcements in the latest gaming news cycle.

items.title: Valve’s Steam Machine pricing reportedly ranges from €1,039 to €1,428
items.summary: A new report says Valve’s Steam Machine will cost between €1,039 and €1,428, depending on configuration. If accurate, the pricing positions it as a premium hardware offering.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth reportedly falls far short of Microsoft targets
items.summary: IGN reports that Microsoft expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers by now, but current reports put it around 30 million. Xbox leadership has reportedly acknowledged that the strategy has not grown as planned.

items.title: Sony signals a shift away from physical PlayStation discs
items.summary: Sony has drawn attention for its move toward a more digital PlayStation future, with reporting indicating new games after January 2028 will be digital-only. The decision has also sparked consumer backlash and related legal scrutiny.

items.title: Nintendo of Europe will stop selling the original Switch in 2027
items.summary: VGC reports that Nintendo will end sales of the original Switch on its European store in February 2027. The move is part of a broader transition toward newer hardware.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 passes 1 million copies sold
items.summary: 11 bit studios says Frostpunk 2 has now sold 1 million copies across all platforms. The milestone was shared alongside a thank-you message to fans.

items.title: Ubisoft announces The Crew Motorfest for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Ubisoft has announced that The Crew Motorfest will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 8, 2026. Physical retail editions will include a digital download code.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown in September
items.summary: Nintendo has confirmed that Mario Kart Tour will shut down on September 29, 2026, and no offline version will be offered. The game has already started winding down in-app purchases.

items.title: Xbox layoffs reportedly hit id Software and Obsidian
items.summary: VGC reports that Microsoft’s latest round of layoffs significantly affected id Software’s coding team and cut 60 to 70 developers from Obsidian. The cuts are part of a broader restructuring inside Xbox.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting previous levies of 7.5% and 5%. The change could benefit manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple deepens Broadcom chipmaking tie-up with more than $30 billion commitment
items.summary: Apple plans to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado. The move is part of Apple’s broader push to secure more U.S.-based chip capacity.

items.title: Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 workers, with most cuts at Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft is cutting about 3,200 jobs across its Xbox business as part of a restructuring effort. The company is shifting resources toward artificial intelligence and away from parts of its gaming division.

items.title: Google loses final EU appeal against record antitrust fine
items.summary: Google lost its last legal bid to overturn the European Union’s record $4.7 billion antitrust fine over alleged abusive practices. The ruling is another major setback for Big Tech in Europe.

items.title: EU court rejects Apple’s challenge to DMA gatekeeper designation
items.summary: The EU General Court dismissed Apple’s legal challenge to its designation as a Digital Markets Act gatekeeper for the App Store and iOS. The decision preserves regulatory obligations on one of Apple’s core platforms.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta plans to build its first Canadian data center in Alberta, a 1GW facility expected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to construct. The project underscores continued heavy infrastructure spending by major tech firms.

items.title: Blue Origin reportedly seeks $10 billion funding round at $130 billion valuation
items.summary: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin is said to be raising its first outside funding round, with reports valuing the rocket company at $130 billion pre-money. The deal would mark a major step for the private space company’s expansion.

items.title: Meta begins manufacturing its own AI chip from September, Reuters reports
items.summary: Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip in September as it works to expand computing power. The internal plan reflects the company’s growing investment in custom hardware.
